label: lem:edge-potential
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Gradient structure and phase symmetry

title: Proof
body_md:
Differentiation and the chain rule give \eqref{eq:full-gradient-components}
	and \eqref{eq:full-gradient-step}.  Reversing an edge changes the signs of
	both $b_e$ and $b_e^T\theta$; evenness of $\Phi_e$ preserves the
	potential, and oddness of $g_e$ preserves the map.  The only freedom in
	the construction is the additive constant in each primitive.  Finally,
	$B^T\mathbf 1=0$ gives \eqref{eq:F-rotation}, and $\mathbf 1^TB=0$ gives the
	orthogonality and \eqref{eq:sum-conserved}.

label: thm:finite-estimates
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Descent and invertibility

title: Proof
body_md:
Taylor's inequality on the periodic lift, with increment
	\(-h\nabla\mathcal V(\theta)\), and Lemma~\ref{thm:Hessian-bound} give
	the first descent estimate \cite{Nesterov2004}. The identities
	\(\mathcal V=V\circ Q\) and \eqref{eq:chain-gradient} give
	\[
	\|\nabla\mathcal V(\theta)\|^2
	=\nabla V(Q\theta)^TM\nabla V(Q\theta),
	\]
	and hence the reduced estimate. Positive definiteness of \(M\) gives
	strictness.
	
	For \(h<1/\Lambda\), Lemma~\ref{thm:Hessian-bound} shows that every eigenvalue of
	\(D\widetilde F_h=I_{N+1}-hD^2\mathcal V\) is positive. The induced
	torus map is therefore an orientation-preserving local diffeomorphism.
	Its image is open and compact, hence closed, so connectedness makes
	it surjective. The homotopy
	\(\theta\mapsto\theta-th\nabla\mathcal V(\theta)\), \(0\le t\le1\),
	gives degree one. A local diffeomorphism of a compact manifold is a
	covering map, and positive orientation makes this covering one-sheeted
	\cite{Lee2012SmoothManifolds}. Thus \(F_h\) is a global diffeomorphism.
	Its inverse also commutes with common-phase shifts, so it induces
	a diffeomorphism on the quotient.
head: environment

label: cor:common-law
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{cor:common-law}
	If \(g_e=g\) for every edge, then \(W_\beta=\|g'\|_\infty A\), so with
	\(L_a=BAB^T\),
	\[
		\Lambda=\|g'\|_\infty\lambda_{\max}(L_a).
	\]
	In particular, \(\Lambda=(2\pi/P)\lambda_{\max}(L_a)\) for
	\(g(s)=\sin(2\pi s/P)\), and
	\(\Lambda=\lambda_{\max}(L_a)\) for the standard law \(g(s)=\sin s\).
head: environment
name: Common interaction law

label: thm:fixed-critical
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Fixed points and convergence

title: Proof
body_md:
Critical points are fixed by \eqref{eq:reduced-gradient-map}.
	Conversely, a fixed point leaves \(V\) unchanged, so strict descent
	forces criticality. A periodic orbit cannot contain a strict decrease
	and is therefore fixed.
	
	Summing \eqref{eq:reduced-descent} gives
	\[
	c_h\sum_{n=0}^{m-1}\nabla V(x_n)^TM\nabla V(x_n)
	\le V(x_0)-V(x_m).
	\]
	Compactness bounds the right-hand side, so positive definiteness of
	\(M\) gives \(\nabla V(x_n)\to0\). Every accumulation point is
	therefore critical. If the distance to \(\operatorname{Crit}(V)\) did not tend to
	zero, a convergent subsequence at a positive distance from it would
	contradict this conclusion. Also,
	\[
		\operatorname{dist}(x_{n+1},x_n)\le h\|M\nabla V(x_n)\|\longrightarrow0.
	\]
	When the critical set is finite, choose balls around its points with
	pairwise disjoint closures. Their mutual distances have a positive
	lower bound. Eventually the orbit lies in their union and its steps
	are smaller than this bound, so it remains in one ball. Its distance
	to the critical set tends to zero, and hence it converges to that
	ball's critical point.
head: environment

label: thm:Morse-hyperbolic
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Hyperbolicity and Morse index

title: Proof
body_md:
At a non-degenerate critical point, put \(H_p=D^2V(p)\). Then
	\[
		D\bar F_h(p)=I_N-hMH_p.
	\]
	The matrix \(MH_p\) is similar to \(M^{1/2}H_pM^{1/2}\), which is
	symmetric and has the inertia of \(H_p\)
	\cite{HornJohnson2012}. Its eigenvalues \(\mu\) are thus real and
	nonzero. They are also the nonzero eigenvalues of
	\(D^2\mathcal V(\theta)=Q^TH_pQ\), for \(Q\theta=p\), so
	\(|\mu|\le\Lambda\) by Lemma~\ref{thm:Hessian-bound}. For \(0<h<1/\Lambda\), positive \(\mu\)
	give multipliers \(0<1-h\mu<1\), while negative \(\mu\) give
	\(1-h\mu>1\). This proves hyperbolicity, the index formula and the
	classification.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The same multiplier calculation gives \(-1<1-h\mu<1\) for positive
	\(\mu\), and \(1-h\mu>1\) for negative \(\mu\), throughout
	\(0<h<2/\Lambda\). Thus non-degenerate critical points retain
	multipliers off the unit circle in the full descent interval.
head: environment

label: thm:global-dynamics
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Almost-global convergence

title: Proof
body_md:
A Morse function on the compact torus has finitely many critical points,
	so every orbit converges by Proposition~\ref{thm:finite-convergence}.
	At each non-minimum critical point, the local stable manifold has
	dimension less than \(N\) by Proposition~\ref{thm:Morse-hyperbolic} and
	the stable-manifold theorem \cite{HirschPughShub1977}.
	It has zero Lebesgue measure, and global invertibility gives
	\[
	W^s(p)=\bigcup_{k\ge0}\bar F_h^{-k}
	\bigl(W^s_{\mathrm{loc}}(p)\bigr).
	\]
	Every preimage is a smooth submanifold of the same dimension and
	therefore has measure zero \cite{Lee2012SmoothManifolds}.
	The finite union over non-minimum critical points is null.
	All other initial conditions converge to local minima.
head: environment

label: thm:matrix-morse-smale
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: A matrix criterion for Morse--Smale dynamics

label: lem:path-slabs
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:path-slabs}
	Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix-morse-smale}, each set
	\[
	\mathcal S_i=\{z\in\mathbb T^N:
	z_i\in[\pi/2,3\pi/2]\pmod{2\pi}\},
	\qquad i=1,\ldots,N,
	\]
	is forward invariant under $G_{K,h}$.  Equivalently, along any orbit
	$z_n=G_{K,h}^n(z_0)$, with components $z_{i,n}$,
	$\cos z_{i,n}\le0$ implies $\cos z_{i,n+1}\le0$.
head: environment
name: Invariant coordinate slabs

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $i$ and let $s=z_{i,n}\in[\pi/2,3\pi/2]$.  The $i$th component of the
	update is
	\[
	s\longmapsto f(s)+hb,\qquad f(s)=s+hk_{ii}\sin s,\qquad
	b=\sum_{j\ne i}k_{ij}\sin z_{j,n},
	\]
	and $|b|\le\sum_{j\ne i}|k_{ij}|\le k_{ii}$ by
	\eqref{eq:matrix-dominance}.  Since
	$hk_{ii}\le h\lambda_{\max}(K)<1$, the function $f$ is strictly
	increasing and maps $[\pi/2,3\pi/2]$ onto
	$[\pi/2+hk_{ii},\,3\pi/2-hk_{ii}]$.  Hence
	$f(s)+hb\in[\pi/2,3\pi/2]$.
head: environment

label: lem:adjoint-transversality
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Adjoint criterion for transversality

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $E^s_n=T_{z_n}W^s(q)$ and $E^u_n=T_{z_n}W^u(p)$.
	The adjoint equation transports covectors by
	$\eta_{n+1}=A_n^{-T}\eta_n$ and preserves their pairing with solutions of
	$v_{n+1}=A_nv_n$.
	
	We claim that $\eta_n\to0$ as $n\to+\infty$ precisely when $\eta_0$
	vanishes on $E^s_0$.  Choose $C^1$ local coordinates $(s,u)$ near $q$ in
	which its local stable manifold is $\{u=0\}$, using the stable-manifold
	theorem \cite{HirschPughShub1977}.  For all sufficiently large $n$, the
	derivative in these coordinates has the block form
	\[
	\widehat A_n=\begin{pmatrix}\Sigma_n&\Xi_n\\0&\Upsilon_n\end{pmatrix},
	\]
	where $\Sigma_n$ tends to the stable block and $\Upsilon_n$ to the unstable
	block of $DG(q)$.  If $\eta_0$ vanishes on $E^s_0$, invariance of the stable
	tangent spaces makes the transported covector have the form $(0,\beta_n)^T$,
	with $\beta_{n+1}=\Upsilon_n^{-T}\beta_n$.
	The limiting inverse transpose has all eigenvalues inside the unit circle.
	Choose a norm in which its operator norm is less than one.  A uniform
	bound less than one then holds for all sufficiently large $n$.
	The coordinate changes and their inverses have bounded derivatives along
	the convergent orbit, so $\eta_n$ decays exponentially in the original
	coordinates too.
	Conversely, stable tangent vectors evolve through $\Sigma_n$; the same norm
	argument gives their exponential decay.  If $\eta_n\to0$, the constant
	pairing $\eta_n^Tv_n=\eta_0^Tv_0$ must therefore vanish, so $\eta_0$
	vanishes on $E^s_0$.
	
	Applying the same argument to $G^{-1}$ at $p$ identifies backward decay
	with vanishing on $E^u_0$.  Solutions of \eqref{eq:adjoint-criterion}
	therefore correspond exactly to covectors vanishing on $E^s_0 + E^u_0$.
	A nonzero such covector exists precisely when the intersection is not
	transverse.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the observation preceding the theorem, $K$ is positive definite.  Put
	$\lambda=\lambda_{\max}(K)$ and
	$D(z)=\operatorname{diag}(\cos z_1,\ldots,\cos z_N)$.
	The derivative $I_N+hKD(z)$ is similar to the symmetric matrix
	$I_N+hK^{1/2}D(z)K^{1/2}$, whose eigenvalues lie in
	$[1-h\lambda,1+h\lambda]\subset(0,2)$.  Thus $G_{K,h}$ is a local
	diffeomorphism.  It is homotopic to the identity through
	$z\mapsto z+thK\sin z$, $0\le t\le1$, and hence has degree one.
	Compactness and positivity of the Jacobian determinant make it a
	one-sheeted covering, so it is a global diffeomorphism. 
	
	The interval \eqref{eq:matrix-ms-range} cannot be enlarged.  Consider the
	diagonal points $z(t)=t\mathbf 1_N$, $t\in[0,\pi]$, where
	$D(z(t))=\cos t\,I_N$ and hence $DG_{K,h}(z(t))=I_N+h\cos t\,K$.  If
	$Kv=\lambda v$ with $v\neq0$, then $DG_{K,h}(z(t))\,v=(1+h\lambda\cos t)\,v$
	for every $t$.  If $h\lambda\ge1$, the number
	$t_*=\arccos\bigl(-1/(h\lambda)\bigr)$ lies in $(\pi/2,\pi]$, and
	$DG_{K,h}(z(t_*))\,v=0$, so $G_{K,h}$ is not a local diffeomorphism.
	
	Since $\|D^2V_0\|_2\le1$ and $\|Kv\|^2\le\lambda\,v^TKv$ for
	$v\in\mathbb R^N$, Taylor's inequality on a real lift gives
	\begin{equation}
		\label{eq:matrix-ms-descent}
		V_0(G_{K,h}(z))-V_0(z)
		\le-h\left(1-\frac{h\lambda}{2}\right)
		(\sin z)^T K\sin z.
	\end{equation}
	Therefore $V_0$ decreases strictly unless $\sin z=0$, and the fixed points
	are exactly $\{0,\pi\}^N$.
	At a fixed point $p$, the matrix $KD(p)$ is similar to
	$K^{1/2}D(p)K^{1/2}$.  By Sylvester's law of inertia, the number of
	positive eigenvalues equals the number of zero coordinates of $p$.
	All eigenvalues $\mu$ are nonzero and satisfy $|\mu|\le\lambda$, so the
	multipliers $1+h\mu$ lie off the unit circle: positive $\mu$ give
	unstable directions and negative $\mu$ stable ones.  The fixed points
	are therefore hyperbolic, with unstable dimension equal to their number
	of zero coordinates.
	
	For a non-fixed point, continuity gives a neighbourhood $U$ such that
	\[
	\sup_{y\in U}V_0(G_{K,h}(y))<\inf_{y\in U}V_0(y).
	\]
	Monotonicity then gives $G_{K,h}^k(U)\cap U=\varnothing$ for every $k\ge1$.
	Hence the nonwandering set is the stated finite fixed set.
	
	It remains to prove transversality.  The idea is to follow the largest
	coordinate of a decaying adjoint solution: diagonal dominance forces
	that coordinate into an invariant slab, where the adjoint equation
	cannot decrease it, which contradicts decay.
	
	Suppose that an intersection is not transverse.  Along its orbit
	$(z_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$, Lemma~\ref{lem:adjoint-transversality} supplies
	a nonzero solution tending to zero at both ends, with
	\[
		\eta_n=(I_N+hD_nK)\eta_{n+1},
		\qquad D_n=D(z_n).
	\]
	The maximum
	\[
		\rho=\max_{1\le i\le N,\ n\in\mathbb Z}|\eta_{i,n}|>0
	\]
	is attained.  Fix a time $j$ at which it is attained, and let
	$\mathcal I=\{i:|\eta_{i,j}|=\rho\}$.
	For $i\in\mathcal I$, put $s_i=\eta_{i,j}/\rho\in\{-1,1\}$.
	Diagonal dominance gives
	\[
	s_i(K\eta_j)_i
	\ge\rho\left(k_{ii}-\sum_{\ell\ne i}|k_{i\ell}|\right)\ge0.
	\]
	For at least one $i\in\mathcal I$ the left side is strictly positive.
	Otherwise, equality forces $k_{i\ell}=0$ for every
	$i\in\mathcal I$ and $\ell\notin\mathcal I$: a nonzero such entry
	would multiply a coordinate of absolute value strictly less than $\rho$.
	It would follow that
	$K_{\mathcal I\mathcal I}(\eta_j)_{\mathcal I}=0$,
	contradicting positive definiteness of this principal submatrix.
	
	Choose such an index $i$ and put $s=s_i$.
	Write $c_{i,n}=\cos z_{i,n}$.  The adjoint equation at time $j-1$ gives
	\[
	s\eta_{i,j-1}
	=\rho+hc_{i,j-1}s(K\eta_j)_i\le\rho,
	\]
	so $c_{i,j-1}\le0$.  Lemma~\ref{lem:path-slabs} implies
	$c_{i,n}\le0$ for every $n\ge j-1$.
	Set $c=c_{i,j}\le0$.  The diagonal coefficient $1+hk_{ii}c$ is strictly
	positive, and the adjoint equation at time $j$ gives
	\begin{align*}
		\rho
		&=(1+hk_{ii}c)s\eta_{i,j+1}
		+hc\sum_{\ell\ne i}k_{i\ell}s\eta_{\ell,j+1}\\
		&\le\rho\left[1+hc
		\left(k_{ii}-\sum_{\ell\ne i}|k_{i\ell}|\right)\right]
		\le\rho.
	\end{align*}
	Equality and the strictly positive diagonal coefficient force
	$\eta_{i,j+1}=s\rho$.  This step uses only $|\eta_{i,n}|=\rho$ and
	$c_{i,n}\le0$, so repeating it forces $\eta_{i,n}=s\rho$ for all
	$n\ge j$, contrary to decay.  This proves transversality.
	
	Finally, \eqref{eq:matrix-ms-descent}, compactness and finiteness of the
	critical set give convergence of every orbit to one fixed point by the
	argument of Proposition~\ref{thm:finite-convergence}.
	The unique minimum is $(\pi,\ldots,\pi)$.  All other fixed points have
	stable manifolds of dimension less than $N$, so their basins have measure
	zero, as in Theorem~\ref{thm:global-dynamics}.
head: environment

label: prop:sharpK
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{prop:sharpK}
	The optimality argument applies to every matrix $K$ similar to a
	symmetric one with $\lambda_{\max}(K)>0$: $G_{K,h}$ is not a local
	diffeomorphism when $h\ge1/\lambda_{\max}(K)$.
head: environment

label: rem:sink-threshold
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:sink-threshold}
	Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix-morse-smale}, for
	$h=1/\lambda_{\max}(K)$ the singular point found in the proof is the sink
	$(\pi,\ldots,\pi)$ itself, where $DG_{K,h}(\pi,  \ldots \pi)=I_N-hK$.  For
	$h>2/\lambda_{\max}(K)$ this point has the multiplier
	$1-h\lambda_{\max}(K)<-1$ and is no longer a sink.
head: environment

label: thm:weighted
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Weighted matrix criterion

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $\tilde K=A^{1/2}KA^{1/2}$, which is positive definite since $K$ is.
	   As $A$ and $D(z)=\operatorname{diag}(\cos z_1,\ldots,\cos z_N)$ are diagonal, $A^{1/2}KAD(z)A^{-1/2}=\tilde KD(z)$.
	Replacing $K$ by $\tilde K$ in the proof of
	Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix-morse-smale} therefore shows that
	$DG_{K,A,h}=I_N+hKAD(z)$ has eigenvalues in
	$[1-h\tilde\lambda,1+h\tilde\lambda]\subset(0,2)$, so that $G_{K,A,h}$
	is a diffeomorphism, and that each point of $\{0,\pi\}^N$ is hyperbolic
	with unstable dimension equal to its number of zero coordinates.  With
	$V_A(z)=\sum_ia_i\cos z_i$ and $u=A\sin z$, the bound
	$u^TKAKu\le\tilde\lambda\,u^TKu$ and Taylor's inequality give
	\[
	V_A(G_{K,A,h}(z))-V_A(z)\le
	-h\Bigl(1-\frac{h\tilde\lambda}{2}\Bigr)u^TKu,
	\]
	which replaces \eqref{eq:matrix-ms-descent}; the fixed points, the
	nonwandering set and the basin follow as before.
	
	The $i$th component of the map is $z_i+hk_{ii}a_i\sin z_i+hb$ with
	$|b|\le k_{ii}a_i$ by \eqref{eq:weighted-dominance}, and
	$hk_{ii}a_i=h\tilde K_{ii}<1$.  Hence the proof of
	Lemma~\ref{lem:path-slabs} applies, and the slabs $\mathcal S_i$ are
	forward invariant.  The adjoint equation is now
	$\eta_n=(I_N+hD_nAK)\eta_{n+1}$: its $i$th row is that of the proof of
	Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix-morse-smale}, with $hc_{i,n}$ multiplied by
	$a_i>0$.  The maximum argument uses \eqref{eq:matrix-dominance} for $K$,
	positive definiteness of $K$, and positivity of the diagonal coefficient
	$1+ha_ik_{ii}c$, so it applies unchanged and proves transversality.
head: environment

label: thm:general-tree-factorisation
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Critical points on trees

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix the phase of vertex $N+1$.  Every other vertex is joined to its
	parent by a unique edge, and its phase is recovered from its parent's by
	adding or subtracting that edge difference.  Hence $\theta\mapsto
	B^T\theta$ induces a bijection from the quotient onto $\mathbb T_P^N$.  Since the
	inverse uses only additions and subtractions, the matrix $C=B^TS$ of
	\eqref{eq:reduced-matrices} has an integer inverse, so $\det C=\pm1$ (that is, $C$ is unimodular) and
	$z=Cx$ is a linear automorphism of $\mathbb T_P^N$ that preserves Lebesgue
	measure.  This proves the coordinate claim, and $V_T(B^T\theta)
	=\mathcal V(\theta)$ gives the potential.  Applying $B^T$ to
	\eqref{eq:network} gives the reduced map.  The Hessian of $V_T$ is
	diagonal, with entries $a_e\Phi_e''(z_e)$, so the critical set, indices
	and minima follow coordinate by coordinate.  The dynamical conclusion is
	Theorem~\ref{thm:global-dynamics}, transported to the $z$ coordinates by
	the automorphism $z=Cx$.
head: environment

label: thm:tree
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Sinusoidal trees

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Proposition~\ref{thm:general-tree-factorisation} to
	$\Phi_e=\cos$, whose critical points $0$ and $\pi$ have second
	derivatives $-1$ and $1$, respectively; here
	$\Lambda=\lambda_{\max}(L_a)$ by \eqref{eq:sin-general-potential}.
head: environment

label: cor:tree-sharp
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:tree-sharp}
	For a sinusoidal tree with positive weights, both bounds of
	Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-estimates} are optimal.  For $h\ge1/\Lambda$ the
	reduced map is not a local diffeomorphism.  For $h>2/\Lambda$ phase
	opposition is not a sink, and strict descent fails near it.
head: environment
name: Optimal step sizes on trees

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{thm:general-tree-factorisation}, the reduced map is
	$z\mapsto z+hB^TBA\sin z$.  Since $B$ has full column rank, $B^TBA$ is
	similar to the positive definite matrix $A^{1/2}B^TBA^{1/2}$, so
	$\lambda_{\max}(B^TBA)=\lambda_{\max}(L_a)=\Lambda>0$, and
	Remark~\ref{prop:sharpK} gives the first claim.  At $(\pi,\ldots,\pi)$
	the derivative is $I_N-hB^TBA$, with multiplier $1-h\Lambda<-1$ for
	$h>2/\Lambda$; a second-order expansion of $V_T$, whose Hessian there
	is $A$, shows that $V_T$ increases along the corresponding eigendirection.
head: environment

label: thm:path
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Sinusoidal paths

title: Proof
body_md:
The matrix $K_N$ is nonsingular, since $B$ has full column rank, and
	weakly diagonally dominant, so Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix-morse-smale}
	applies.  Since $\lambda_{\max}(K_N)<4$ for finite $N$, $h=1/4$ is
	included.
head: environment

label: cor:star-morse-smale
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:star-morse-smale}
	For four oscillators on the unit-weight star $\mathsf K_{1,3}$, with one centre
	joined to three leaves, the reduced sinusoidal map is Morse--Smale for
	$0<h<1/4$.  It has eight fixed points: one sink, three of unstable
	dimension one, three of unstable dimension two, and one source.
head: environment
name: The star with three leaves

title: Proof
body_md:
Orienting all edges from the centre gives the weakly diagonally dominant
	matrix
	\[
		K=B^TB=\begin{pmatrix}2&1&1\\1&2&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix},
		\qquad \operatorname{spec}(K)=\{1,1,4\},
	\]
	which is nonsingular. The result follows from direct application of  Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix-morse-smale}.
head: environment

label: cor:wpath
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Weighted paths

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{thm:general-tree-factorisation}, the reduced map is
	$G_{K_N,A,h}$, with $K_N$ as in \eqref{eq:path-gradient}, and
	\eqref{eq:concave} is \eqref{eq:weighted-dominance}.  The matrix
	$A^{1/2}K_NA^{1/2}=(BA^{1/2})^T(BA^{1/2})$ has the nonzero spectrum of
	$BAB^T=L_a$, so $\tilde\lambda=\lambda_{\max}(L_a)$.
	Theorem~\ref{thm:weighted} applies, and optimality is
	Corollary~\ref{cor:tree-sharp}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The weights $a_i=\sin\bigl(i\pi/(N+1)\bigr)$ satisfy \eqref{eq:concave}
	strictly, the weights $a_i=i$ satisfy it with equality for $i<N$, and
	geometric weights $a_i=r^i$, $r\ne1$, violate it.  For paths the
	admissible weights thus form a closed convex cone with nonempty
	interior, an explicit open set of Morse--Smale weights.  Unit weights lie
	on its boundary, so this complements the non-explicit neighbourhood of
	Corollary~\ref{cor:hamiltonian-morse-smale}.  Strict dominance of $K$ in
	some row is essential: by symmetry of $K$,
	\[
	\sum_{i=1}^N\Bigl(k_{ii}a_i-\sum_{j\ne i}|k_{ij}|a_j\Bigr)
	=\sum_{j=1}^Na_j\Bigl(k_{jj}-\sum_{i\ne j}|k_{ij}|\Bigr),
	\]
		so if \eqref{eq:matrix-dominance} is an equality in every row, so is
	\eqref{eq:weighted-dominance}.  For $\mathsf K_{1,3}$ this forces
	$a_1=a_2=a_3$, which only rescales $h$ in
	Corollary~\ref{cor:star-morse-smale}.
head: environment

label: cor:matrix-structural-stability
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:matrix-structural-stability}
	\label{cor:path-structural-stability}
	Fix $K$ and $h$ satisfying the hypotheses of
	Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix-morse-smale}.  There is a $C^1$ neighbourhood
	$\mathcal U$ of $G_{K,h}$ in the space of $C^1$ diffeomorphisms of
	$\mathbb T^N$ such that every $\widehat G\in\mathcal U$ is Morse--Smale
	and topologically conjugate to $G_{K,h}$, that is,
	$H\circ G_{K,h}=\widehat G\circ H$ for some homeomorphism
	$H:\mathbb T^N\to\mathbb T^N$.  Each such map has exactly $2^N$ fixed
	points, $\binom Nr$ of unstable dimension $r$, and one sink.
head: environment
name: Structural stability

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply the structural stability theorem for Morse--Smale diffeomorphisms
	\cite{PalisSmale1970} to Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix-morse-smale}.
	Hyperbolic continuation preserves the unstable dimensions of the fixed
	points.
head: environment

label: cor:hamiltonian-morse-smale
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:hamiltonian-morse-smale}
	Let $\mathcal G$ be an undirected graph on $N+1$ vertices containing a
	spanning path $\Pi$. Fix $h$ satisfying \eqref{eq:path-diffeo-range}.  There is
	$\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ such that the reduced sinusoidal map on
	$\mathcal G$ is Morse--Smale and topologically conjugate to the
	unit-weight path map whenever
	\begin{equation}
		\label{eq:hamiltonian-weight-range}
		|a_e-1|<\varepsilon\quad(e\in\Pi),
		\qquad
		0<a_e<\varepsilon\quad(e\notin\Pi).
	\end{equation}
	In particular, these positive weights form an open set of parameters with
	exactly $2^N$ fixed points and one sink.
head: environment
name: Graphs containing a spanning path

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $a_e=1$ on $\Pi$ and $a_e=0$ on the remaining edges.  This is the
	path map of Corollary~\ref{thm:path-morse-smale}, expressed in the
	reference-phase coordinates of Section~\ref{sec:reciprocal-gradient};
	by Proposition~\ref{thm:general-tree-factorisation} the two coordinate
	systems differ by a linear automorphism of the torus, so the map is
	Morse--Smale in either.  The reduced map depends continuously in $C^1$ on
	all edge weights, and
	Corollary~\ref{cor:matrix-structural-stability} therefore supplies
	$\varepsilon$ with the stated property.
head: environment

label: rem:sinusoidal-sign-conjugacy
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:sinusoidal-sign-conjugacy}
	Let $\tau(z)=z+\pi\mathbf 1_N\pmod{2\pi}$.  Then
	\[
	\tau^{-1}\circ G_{K,h}\circ\tau(z)=z-hK\sin z.
	\]
	Consequently, the matrix criterion also applies with the opposite sign
	of the sine interaction.  On a tree, $\tau$ is induced by adding $\pi$
	to the vertex phases in one bipartition class.
	The path and three-leaf-star results therefore also give structural
	stability for $g(s)=-\sin s$, whose unique sink is the equal-phase state.
	The weak-link corollary holds for that sign too, by perturbing the
	corresponding path map.
head: environment
name: The two signs of sinusoidal interaction

label: prop:tree-sign-obstruction
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: A tree obstruction to transversality

title: Proof
body_md:
Orient every edge from one bipartition class to the other and set
	$K=B^TB$ and $d=(d_e)_{e\in\mathcal E}$.  The diagonal entries of $K$ are
	two, and its off-diagonal entries are one when the edges share a vertex
	and zero otherwise.  For an edge $uv$, \eqref{eq:tree-sign-condition}
	gives
	\[
	(Kd)_{uv}=\sum_{e\ni u}d_e+\sum_{e\ni v}d_e=2.
	\]
	Put $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(d_e)$ and let $p_e=0$ if $d_e=1$, and
	$p_e=\pi$ if $d_e=-1$.  Writing $m$ for the number of edges and
	$\mathbf 1_m=(1,\ldots,1)^T$, the circle $z(s)=p+s\mathbf 1_m$ is invariant,
	with induced map $s\mapsto s+2h\sin s$.
	The bound on $h$ implies $h<1/2$, since $\lambda_{\max}(K)\ge2$.
	For $0<s<\pi$, the scalar map is strictly increasing and maps this
	interval into itself.  Since $s+2h\sin s>s$ there, every orbit has
	forward limit $\pi$ and backward limit zero.
	Thus the arc joins $p$ to its binary complement
	$q=p+\pi\mathbf 1_m\pmod{2\pi}$.
	
	Along the arc, the derivative is $I_m+h\cos s\,K\Delta$.
	The matrix $K\Delta$ is similar to the symmetric matrix
	$K^{1/2}\Delta K^{1/2}$.  Sylvester's law of inertia shows that
	$K\Delta$ has $m-r$ positive and $r$ negative eigenvalues.  Every
	eigenvalue $\mu$ satisfies $|\mu|\le\lambda_{\max}(K)$.  All variational
	factors $1+h\mu\cos s$ are therefore positive, and the same real
	eigenspaces are preserved along the orbit.  Let $E_+$ be the sum of the
	positive eigenspaces of $K\Delta$.
	
	Tangent vectors to $W^u(p)$ decay under backward iteration of the
	derivative.  A nonzero component in a negative eigenspace instead grows
	backwards, because its forward multiplier tends to $1+h\mu\in(0,1)$
	near $p$.  Hence $T_zW^u(p)\subseteq E_+$, and equality follows from the
	dimensions.  Similarly, negative eigendirections grow forwards near $q$,
	where their multipliers tend to $1-h\mu>1$.  Thus
	\begin{equation}
		\label{eq:tree-obstruction-tangents}
		T_zW^u(p)=T_zW^s(q)=E_+.
	\end{equation}
	A negative sign makes $E_+$ a proper subspace, so the intersection is
	not transverse.
	
	Finally, summing \eqref{eq:tree-sign-condition} over vertices gives
	$2(m-2r)=m+1$, since a tree has $m+1$ vertices.  Therefore $m=4r+1$,
	and Sylvester's law gives $\dim E_+=m-r=3r+1$.
head: environment

label: prop:tree-nontransverse
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Six-vertex tree counterexample

label: eq:tree-counterexample-map
title: Proof
body_md:
Label the vertices $1,\ldots,6$ and orient and order the edges as
\[
    (1,2),\quad(1,3),\quad(1,4),\quad(5,2),\quad(6,2),
\]
where the first vertex is the tail and the second is the head.
In edge coordinates,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:tree-counterexample-map}
    G_{K_*,h}(z)=z+hK_*\sin z\pmod{2\pi},\qquad
    K_*=B^TB=
    \begin{pmatrix}
      2&1&1&1&1\\
      1&2&1&0&0\\
      1&1&2&0&0\\
      1&0&0&2&1\\
      1&0&0&1&2
    \end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
The signs $d=(-1,1,1,1,1)^T$ satisfy
\eqref{eq:tree-sign-condition}.  The eigenvalues of $K_*$ are
$1,1,3,(5-\sqrt{17})/2$ and $(5+\sqrt{17})/2$, so
Proposition~\ref{prop:tree-sign-obstruction} applies in the stated range.
Explicitly, with
\[
    p=(\pi,0,0,0,0)^T,\qquad q=(0,\pi,\pi,\pi,\pi)^T,
\]
the arc $z(s)=p+s\mathbf 1_5$, $0<s<\pi$, has scalar dynamics
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:tree-counterexample-circle}
    s(n+1)=s(n)+2h\sin s(n).
\end{equation}
For $\Delta_*=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1,1)$, the sum of the eigenspaces
of $K_*\Delta_*$ corresponding to positive eigenvalues is
\[
    E_+=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^5:
               4\xi_1=\xi_2+\xi_3+\xi_4+\xi_5\}.
\]
It equals both tangent spaces along this heteroclinic arc by
\eqref{eq:tree-obstruction-tangents}.

title: Proposition
head: environment
name: All-to-all interaction

title: Proof
body_md:
Expand $|Z|^2$ to obtain \eqref{eq:all-potential-order}.  Equally spaced
	phases have $Z=0$, so the squared-modulus formula identifies the minimum
	and all its minimisers.
